item.aggregated_output:
===== abfs-rename-metadata-recovery.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18242. ABFS Rename Failure when tracking metadata is in an incomplete state
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  ABFS users need rename to recover safely when metadata is left in an incomplete intermediate state rather than returning a confusing partial result.

  ## Desired outcome

  Rename should distinguish recovery from hard failure, preserve the final source/destination outcome, and expose operational counters for `rename_recovery`, `metadata_incomplete_rename_failures`, and `rename_path_attempts`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Successful recovery leaves the destination present and source absent, failed recovery is surfaced clearly, and the new rename statistics reflect what actually happened.

  '

===== active-tailer-jn-tolerance.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16689. NameNode may crash when transitioning to Active with in-progress tailer if there are some abnormal JNs.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  During HA failover, a NameNode transitioning to active can still have an in-progress edit tailer, and abnormal JournalNodes in that window can trigger crashes instead of a controlled recovery path.


  ## Desired outcome

  Transitioning to active should tolerate abnormal JournalNode stream conditions during in-progress tailing without crashing the NameNode. Operators should see the transition either complete safely or fail in a controlled way, rather than losing the process because the tailer cannot handle the JournalNode state.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The edit-tailing path should be able to distinguish the durable-only case and avoid taking the NameNode down when JournalNode streams are abnormal during activation. HA transition behavior should remain stable for healthy JournalNodes.

  '

===== aliyun-oss-tempfile-deletion.yaml =====
title: 'HADOOP-18313: AliyunOSSBlockOutputStream should not mark the temporary file for deletion'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using the Aliyun OSS connector expect upload temp files to behave like ordinary local scratch files, without surprising JVM shutdown cleanup that can interfere with local buffer management.


  ## Desired outcome

  Temp files created for OSS writes should still be placed in the configured local buffer directories, but they should no longer be registered for delete-on-exit cleanup.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A temp file created for an OSS write exists under a configured buffer directory, is not tracked for automatic deletion at JVM exit, and repeated creations still distribute across the configured local buffer locations.

  '

===== blockmanager-constructor-checkstyle.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16553 Fix checkstyle for the length of BlockManager construction method over limit.
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The `BlockManager` constructor has grown past the project''s style limits, making one of HDFS''s core initialization paths harder to read and maintain. This is internal cleanup in a critical subsystem, not a behavior change request.


  ## Desired outcome

  The constructor setup should be refactored into smaller initialization steps so the code meets the existing style constraints while preserving the exact same validation, configuration loading, and startup behavior. Any exceptions for invalid replication-related settings and the initial configuration logging should remain unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `BlockManager` initialization is split into cleaner internal setup routines, the constructor no longer violates the length limit, the same configuration checks and error conditions still occur, and NameNode startup behavior is otherwise unchanged.

  '

===== bzip2-split-extra-record.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18321.Fix when to read an additional record from a BZip2 text file split
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Split-based text processing over BZip2 inputs depends on consistent record ownership at block boundaries, and extra reads in the wrong boundary cases can duplicate or over-consume records.


  ## Desired outcome

  BZip2 split readers should read one extra record only in the boundary cases that are actually required to preserve complete record delivery across splits, for both mapred and mapreduce line readers.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Record counts remain correct when splits start or end just before, at, or just after a BZip2 block boundary, instead of duplicating or over-reading records around those transitions.

  '

===== cli-missing-user-warnings.yaml =====
title: 'HADOOP-18306: Warnings should not be shown on cli console when linux user not present on client'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Routine Hadoop CLI commands can emit a warning when the local Linux user is unavailable for group lookup even though that condition is often non-fatal, which adds noisy output for users and operators.


  ## Desired outcome

  The missing-local-user detail should remain available for troubleshooting, but it should be logged at a debug-oriented level rather than as a visible warning during normal CLI use.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Typical CLI runs no longer print that warning, while the same diagnostic detail is still available when debug logging is enabled.

  '

===== corrupt-replica-invalidation-threshold.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16064. Determine when to invalidate corrupt replicas based on number of usable replicas
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The NameNode can keep corrupt replicas around longer than necessary when it bases invalidation only on live replicas, even if there are enough other usable replicas on decommissioning or entering-maintenance nodes.


  ## Desired outcome

  Corrupt replica invalidation should be driven by the full set of usable replicas so the NameNode can remove bad copies once the block is still safely recoverable.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Blocks with adequate usable redundancy are no longer held back from corrupt-replica cleanup solely because some healthy replicas are not counted as live, and decommissioning can continue instead of stalling on that condition.

  '

===== defined-directive-if-checks.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16602. Use "defined" directive along with #if'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  This is preprocessor hygiene in the native compatibility layer rather than a behavior change.

  ## Desired outcome

  Windows type detection should use `defined(_WIN64)` and `defined(_WIN32)` in `#if` checks so the compatibility header evaluates correctly under stricter preprocessors.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The same `ssize_t` behavior is preserved, with cleaner cross-platform preprocessing.

  '

===== delegation-token-expiry-test.yaml =====
title: YARN-11172. Fix TestClientRMTokens#testDelegationToken introduced by HDFS-16563.
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A YARN client using an expired delegation token should receive a clear expired-token failure, but formatting drift in the returned message makes token expiry handling inconsistent and harder to diagnose.


  ## Desired outcome

  Expired delegation token requests should continue to fail as `InvalidToken`, and the returned message should clearly state that the token has expired.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A request made with an expired delegation token is rejected with an `InvalidToken` error whose message explicitly identifies the token as expired.

  '

===== ec-decoding-concurrent-preads.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16422. Fix thread safety of EC decoding during concurrent preads
category: bugfix
requirement: 'HDFS-16422. Fix thread safety of EC decoding during concurrent preads


  Reading data on an erasure-coded file with missing replicas(internal block of block group) will cause online reconstruction: read `dataUnits` part of data and decode them into the target missing data. Each `DFSStripedInputStream` object has a `RawErasureDecoder` object, and when we doing pread concurrently, `RawErasureDecoder.decode` will be invoked concurrently too. `RawErasureDecoder.decode` is not thread safe, as a result of that we get wrong data from pread occasionally.

  '

===== ec-decommission-performance.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16613. EC: Improve performance of decommissioning dn with many ec blocks'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Decommissioning a DataNode in an erasure-coded HDFS cluster can take longer than necessary when recovery work for that node is throttled like ordinary replication traffic.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should allow decommissioning datanodes to use the hard replication stream limit for erasure-coded recovery so that decommission progress is not capped by the normal stream setting.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Operators decommissioning datanodes that host many EC blocks see faster progress without having to increase the general replication stream limit for the whole cluster.

  '

===== ec-reconstruction-source-check.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16479. EC: NameNode should not send a reconstruction work when the source datanodes are insufficient'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  In erasure-coded HDFS, the NameNode can currently schedule reconstruction work even when there are not enough usable source DataNodes to rebuild the missing data. That creates pointless work assignments which fail downstream and surface avoidable reconstruction errors on the DataNode side.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should skip issuing EC reconstruction work when the set of non-busy source DataNodes is insufficient to recover the missing stripes. Reconstruction should still be scheduled normally once enough valid sources are available, but impossible work should be filtered out before it is sent.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Reconstruction work is not dispatched when too few usable EC sources remain, no failing work item is generated for those impossible cases, eligible blocks are still scheduled once enough sources are available, and the affected under-reconstruction blocks remain tracked without triggering avoidable DataNode-side failures.

  '

===== ec-single-dn-rack-decommission.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16456. EC: Decommission a rack with only on dn will fail when the rack number is equal with replication'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators using erasure coding can get stuck decommissioning a DataNode when a rack has only one node and the cluster has about as many racks as the EC placement expects. In that layout, the decommission workflow can incorrectly conclude that placement cannot be satisfied, even though the cluster should be able to rebalance across the remaining non-empty racks.


  ## Desired outcome

  Decommissioning should continue to work for EC data when a single-node rack is being drained, including cases where rack count and replica-placement limits would otherwise be calculated too strictly. Placement decisions should treat empty racks appropriately, fall back to other valid racks when an initial choice fails, and keep block placement policy satisfaction intact through the decommission process.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A DataNode can be decommissioned successfully from a one-node rack in the affected EC topology, replacement replicas are still created with valid rack distribution, non-empty rack accounting stays correct as nodes are decommissioned or recommissioned, and placement-policy checks no longer fail solely because an emptied rack is still counted against the cluster layout.

  '

===== external-sps-jmx-metrics.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16488. [SPS]: Expose metrics to JMX for external SPS'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators using the external Storage Policy Satisfier need standard JMX visibility into what that service is doing instead of relying only on logs.

  ## Desired outcome

  External SPS should publish a stable monitoring surface through `ExternalSPSMXBean`, backed by `ExternalSPSBeanMetrics`, so operators can inspect attempted movement state and related activity from ordinary JMX tooling.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The external SPS process initializes and closes its metrics cleanly, and the JMX surface exposes the attempted-item data needed for monitoring.

  '

===== federation-application-update-apis.yaml =====
title: YARN-11159. Support failApplicationAttempt, updateApplicationPriority, updateApplicationTimeouts API's for Federation
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  In a federated YARN deployment, administrators expect the router to support the same application-management operations they can issue against a single ResourceManager, but some update flows still stop at the federation boundary.


  ## Desired outcome

  The router should forward `failApplicationAttempt`, `updateApplicationPriority`, and `updateApplicationTimeouts` to the owning subcluster and expose normal success, failure, and latency accounting for those operations.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A federated client can invoke all three APIs through the router and get the same operational result it would expect from a non-federated path, while router metrics show whether each request succeeded, failed, and how long it took.

  '

===== federation-client-api-support.yaml =====
title: YARN-10487. Support getQueueUserAcls, listReservations, getApplicationAttempts, getContainerReport, getContainers, getResourceTypeInfo API's for Federation
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Developers integrating with a federated YARN router expect the same breadth of read-only client APIs they already use against a single cluster.

  ## Desired outcome

  Federation should support `getQueueUserAcls`, `listReservations`, `getApplicationAttempts`, `getContainerReport`, `getContainers`, and `getResourceTypeInfo`, including response merging plus success, failure, and latency metrics for each path.

  ## Acceptance signals

  These APIs return federated results through the router instead of a not-implemented path, and their counters appear alongside the existing router metrics.

  '

===== federation-node-attributes-apis.yaml =====
title: YARN-11161. Support getAttributesToNodes, getClusterNodeAttributes, getNodesToAttributes API's for Federation
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Federated YARN users can already ask the Router for many cluster-wide views, but node attribute APIs still stop at the single-cluster boundary, which makes fleet-wide scheduling diagnostics incomplete.


  ## Desired outcome

  The federated client path should support `getAttributesToNodes`, `getClusterNodeAttributes`, and `getNodesToAttributes` end to end so callers can retrieve cluster-wide node-attribute views from the Router instead of querying each ResourceManager separately. The Router must also publish success, failure, and latency accounting for these three operations so operators can see whether those federated lookups are healthy.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The Router should aggregate attribute data returned from multiple subclusters into the expected API responses for `getAttributesToNodes`, `getClusterNodeAttributes`, and `getNodesToAttributes`. Router metrics must expose counters and latency tracking for those exact operation names, including `getNumSucceededGetAttributesToNodesRetrieved`, `getNumSucceededGetClusterNodeAttributesRetrieved`, `getNumSucceededGetNodesToAttributesRetrieved`, and the corresponding failed-retrieval counters.

  '

===== federation-proxy-failover.yaml =====
title: YARN-11237. Fix Bug while disabling proxy failover with Federation
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In federated YARN setups, disabling classic RM HA failover should not accidentally disable the separate federation failover path, but the proxy provider currently ties those decisions together too loosely.


  ## Desired outcome

  Failover handling should continue to work when federation failover is enabled, even if RM HA auto-failover is turned off. The decision point needs to respect the federation-specific setting so Router and federation-aware clients do not lose failover protection just because non-federated HA failover is disabled.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A configuration with `FEDERATION_ENABLED=true`, `FEDERATION_FAILOVER_ENABLED=true`, and `AUTO_FAILOVER_ENABLED=false` should still report failover as enabled for the federation-aware proxy path. Non-federated behavior should remain unchanged.

  '

===== federation-queue-api-support.yaml =====
title: YARN-11169. Support moveApplicationAcrossQueues, getQueueInfo API's for Federation.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A federated YARN deployment should let administrators inspect queues and move applications through the router just as they would against a single ResourceManager, but those flows are still incomplete.


  ## Desired outcome

  The router should support both `getQueueInfo` and `moveApplicationAcrossQueues`, including normal success, failure, and latency metrics for those federated operations.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Federated clients can retrieve queue details and move applications across queues through the router, and the router''s metrics surface reflects successful and failed handling of both APIs.

  '

===== federation-resource-profile-apis.yaml =====
title: YARN-11160. Support getResourceProfiles, getResourceProfile API's for Federation
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A federated YARN deployment should expose the same resource-profile discovery features as a single-cluster deployment, but the router still lacks support for those profile lookups.

  The router should support both `getResourceProfiles` and `getResourceProfile`, merging the participating subcluster responses into normal federation-level results and recording success, failure, and latency metrics for those APIs.

  '

===== hdfs-find-cross-platform.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16470. Make HDFS find tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_find` command currently depends on Linux-only argument parsing, which makes the tool unavailable or unreliable on other platforms even though the underlying file search workflow is otherwise portable. Developers using the native client need the same basic find behavior regardless of operating system.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_find` should work cross-platform while preserving the existing command-line experience for searching from a start path, filtering by `-n`, and limiting traversal depth with `-m`. This is a portability fix, so the tool''s observable search behavior should stay the same while its option parsing becomes usable beyond Linux.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_find` runs on non-Linux platforms, still accepts the expected path and filtering options, and produces the same search results users would expect from the current Linux implementation.

  '

===== hdfs-ls-cross-platform.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16471. Make HDFS ls tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_ls` tool is tied to Linux-only option parsing today, which makes a basic file-listing command unnecessarily platform-specific for developers using the native client. Teams working on Windows or other non-Linux environments still need the same listing and recursive inspection workflow.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_ls` should become cross-platform without changing the user-visible command semantics, including normal listing and recursive traversal with `-R`. The portability work must preserve the current output behavior so users can keep the same scripts and expectations while gaining non-Linux support.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_ls` works on supported non-Linux platforms, still honors the existing path and `-R` behavior, and produces the same style of listing results users already rely on.

  '

===== hdfs-setrep-cross-platform.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16472. Make HDFS setrep tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_setrep` tool currently depends on Linux-only option parsing, which makes replication-management workflows unnecessarily platform-specific for teams using the native client on other operating systems. Operators and developers still need the same ability to change replication on files and recursively across directory trees regardless of platform.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_setrep` should work cross-platform while preserving its current command-line behavior for setting a target replication factor on a path and applying that change recursively when a directory is provided. This is a portability update, so the tool''s observable replication-changing behavior should remain the same while the argument parsing becomes usable beyond Linux.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_setrep` runs on supported non-Linux platforms, still accepts the existing replication-factor and path arguments, continues to handle directory recursion as before, and changes replication in the same way users already expect from the Linux implementation.

  '

===== hdfs-sets-helper-removal.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16616. remove use of org.apache.hadoop.util.Sets
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Some HDFS code paths still rely on `org.apache.hadoop.util.Sets` for simple collection creation even though ordinary Java collections already cover those cases.


  ## Desired outcome

  Replace that redundant helper usage in the affected HDFS code with the standard Java collection types while preserving the current semantics and behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Users and operators observe no functional change, and maintainers no longer have to read through an extra helper layer for ordinary set construction.

  '

===== hdfs-stat-cross-platform.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16473. Make HDFS stat tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_stat` tool currently relies on Linux-only option parsing, which keeps a basic metadata-inspection command from working consistently across development platforms. Users of the native client should be able to inspect file or directory status and get the usual error reporting on non-Linux systems too.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_stat` should become cross-platform while preserving its current command-line behavior for files, directories, and missing paths. This is a portability fix, so the tool should keep the same style of stat output and failure reporting while becoming usable beyond Linux.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_stat` runs on supported non-Linux platforms, still reports metadata for both files and directories in the expected format, still surfaces an appropriate error for a missing path, and does not change the observable stat semantics users already rely on.

  '

===== hdfs-tail-cross-platform.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16474. Make HDFS tail tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_tail` tool currently depends on Linux-only option parsing, which prevents teams using the native client on other platforms from relying on the same quick file-inspection workflow. Developers and operators still need to read the tail of an HDFS file, follow appended output, and get the usual failure reporting for missing paths regardless of operating system.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_tail` should become cross-platform while preserving its current command-line behavior, including reading the last portion of a file by default and continuing to follow appended data when `-f` is used. This is a portability fix, so the observable tail output and error semantics should remain the same while argument parsing becomes usable beyond Linux.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_tail` runs on supported non-Linux platforms, still prints the tail of an existing file in the same way as before, continues to support follow mode with `-f`, reports an appropriate error for a missing path, and does not change the user-visible behavior of the tool apart from restoring portability.

  '

===== iostatisticscontext-tuning.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18373. IOStatisticsContext tuning
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The thread-level toggle should use the clearer configuration contract `IOSTATISTICS_THREAD_LEVEL_ENABLED`, and runtime code should be able to ask whether the feature is enabled through `IOStatisticsContextIntegration.isIOStatisticsThreadLevelEnabled()`. Existing default behavior should stay enabled unless explicitly configured otherwise.

  '

===== ipc-multi-connection-throughput.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-13144. Enhancing IPC client throughput via multiple connections per user
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Hadoop service running very high IPC call volumes to the same endpoint can bottleneck on a single client-side connection per user, even when the workload itself is highly parallel.


  ## Desired outcome

  Operators and framework code should be able to open more than one logical client connection for the same address, protocol, and user when they deliberately vary the connection identity, instead of being forced through one shared channel. The public RPC surface needs to make that possible by accepting a caller-supplied `Client.ConnectionId` in `RPC.getProtocolProxy(...)`, so advanced clients can spread traffic without forking the whole RPC stack.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Using `RPC.getProtocolProxy` with distinct `Client.ConnectionId` instances should yield independent client proxies and allow the same principal to drive parallel request streams to one server. Existing call semantics, security initialization, and retry behavior from the `ConnectionId` must remain intact.

  '

===== kubernetes-datanode-locality.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16540 Data locality is lost when DataNode pod restarts in kubern…
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  In Kubernetes-style deployments, a DataNode pod can restart with the same DataNode identity but a different IP address. If the NameNode keeps the old host-to-DataNode mapping around, clients and colocated services can lose data locality because the stale IP is still treated as the preferred host.


  ## Desired outcome

  When a DataNode re-registers with the same UUID but a new IP address, the NameNode should replace the old host mapping with the new one so locality decisions follow the live pod location. This should preserve the existing registration semantics while ensuring stale IP entries do not continue to influence host lookups or block-location ordering.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Re-registration with the same DataNode identity removes the obsolete host entry, the new IP becomes the active host mapping for that DataNode, locality-sensitive block locations prefer the current IP rather than the stale one, and restarting a DataNode pod no longer causes persistent locality loss.

  '

===== libhdfs-openfile-apis.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-14478: Add libhdfs APIs for openFile'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Native HDFS clients need the same richer open-file controls that are available on the Java side, including the ability to construct an open request, set required or optional parameters, and wait on the resulting asynchronous open. Without a public libhdfs surface for that workflow, C consumers cannot participate in newer open-file capabilities cleanly.


  ## Desired outcome

  libhdfs should expose a public open-file builder and future-based API for this workflow. The exported contract needs to include `hdfsOpenFileBuilderAlloc`, `hdfsOpenFileBuilderMust`, `hdfsOpenFileBuilderOpt`, `hdfsOpenFileBuilderBuild`, `hdfsOpenFileBuilderFree`, `hdfsOpenFileFutureGet`, `hdfsOpenFileFutureGetWithTimeout`, `hdfsOpenFileFutureCancel`, and `hdfsOpenFileFutureFree`, so native callers can configure, launch, wait on, cancel, and clean up an open-file request through stable C APIs.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Native callers can allocate an open-file builder, set must and optional parameters, build an asynchronous open request, obtain the resulting file with or without a timeout, cancel an in-flight future when appropriate, and free both builder and future objects through the documented libhdfs API surface.

  '

===== namenode-slow-peer-reconfigure.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16528. Reconfigure slow peer enable for Namenode
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  NameNode operators may want to turn slow-peer tracking on or off while a cluster is running so they can manage diagnostic overhead without taking the NameNode down. Right now the `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` setting is not fully reconfigurable on the NameNode side, which makes that operational toggle less useful than related live-reconfig options.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should allow `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` to be reconfigured at runtime, with slow-peer tracking behavior updating immediately to match the new boolean value. When disabled, slow-peer reports and JSON output should stop surfacing collected data; when enabled again, the normal slow-peer tracker should resume without requiring a restart.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Administrators can reconfigure `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` on a live NameNode, the NameNode switches between enabled and disabled slow-peer tracking behavior immediately, disabled mode returns empty slow-peer results instead of stale data, and invalid non-boolean values are rejected as reconfiguration errors rather than being silently accepted.

  '

===== oiv-ec-policy-output.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16655. OIV: print out erasure coding policy name in oiv Delimited output'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

===== overlapping-range-validation.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18355. Update previous index properly while validating overlapping ranges.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Vectored-read callers rely on early validation to reject overlapping byte ranges, but a bookkeeping bug can leave the validator comparing the wrong prior range and miss a real overlap.


  ## Desired outcome

  `validateNonOverlappingAndReturnSortedRanges` should update its previous-range tracking correctly while it walks the sorted list, so any overlapping pair is rejected reliably. Callers should continue to get the same failure style they already expect for overlapping requests.

  Overlapping ranges must still fail with `UnsupportedOperationException` carrying the message `Overlapping ranges are not supported`, and non-overlapping ranges should continue to be returned in sorted order. The fix should be in validation accuracy, not in changing the API surface.

  '

===== queue-mapping-delete-safety.yaml =====
title: YARN-10287.Update scheduler-conf corrupts the CS configuration when removing queue which is referred in queue mapping

===== rbf-actual-client-ip.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-13248: Namenode needs to use the actual client IP when going through RBF proxy.'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  In Router-based Federation deployments, the NameNode currently sees the router''s address instead of the real client address, which can break locality-sensitive decisions and send reads to less appropriate DataNodes. Operators need a safe way to forward the original client IP without letting arbitrary users spoof it.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should honor client IP information forwarded by trusted router users so data-locality decisions can use the real caller address, but only when that forwarding is allowed by `dfs.namenode.ip-proxy-users`. If the caller is not trusted, the NameNode should continue using the proxy address, and the existing audit-log behavior can remain as it is.


  ## Acceptance signals

  With `dfs.namenode.ip-proxy-users` configured for the router identity, locality decisions prefer replicas near the actual client IP; without that trust, the proxy address is still used; and the feature can be enabled or disabled administratively without changing normal RBF request routing.

  '

===== rbf-dynamic-handler-allocation.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-14750. RBF: Support dynamic handler allocation in routers'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Router-based Federation operators need fairness controls that can adapt handler capacity to real namespace traffic instead of staying fixed after startup. Static allocation can leave busy namespaces short on handlers while quieter namespaces hold unused capacity, which makes router throughput less responsive than it should be under uneven load.


  ## Desired outcome

  RBF should support a `DynamicRouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` that periodically resizes per-namespace permit capacity based on observed traffic while still enforcing configured minimum handler floors. The dynamic controller needs to honor the router handler-count settings, the minimum-per-namespace setting, and the refresh interval configuration, and it should expose the resulting capacity distribution through the existing permit-capacity JSON surface returned by `getPermitCapacityPerNs()` so operators and tests can observe the live allocation.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Routers can instantiate `DynamicRouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` as a fairness-policy option, per-namespace permit capacity is rebalanced over time according to traffic while preserving the configured minimum handler guarantees, the controller reports the current allocation through `getPermitCapacityPerNs()` as JSON, and permit acquisition behavior reflects the updated capacities rather than the static startup allocation.

  '

===== rbf-fairness-policy-reconfigure.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16539. RBF: Support refreshing/changing router fairness policy controller without rebooting router'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators running Router-based Federation may need to change the router fairness policy controller or refresh its handler allocation without bouncing the router process. Requiring a restart for that kind of fairness tuning creates unnecessary disruption and makes it harder to adjust live traffic handling safely.


  ## Desired outcome

  Router fairness policy control should be refreshable at runtime through the existing generic refresh mechanism, including support for changing the configured controller implementation and reloading handler allocation settings without a router reboot. The refresh contract should be exposed through the `RefreshFairnessPolicyController` handler so operators can invoke `hdfs dfsrouteradmin -refreshRouterArgs ROUTER_ADDR RefreshFairnessPolicyController` and have the router begin using the refreshed fairness policy immediately.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A router can refresh its fairness policy controller without restarting, the `RefreshFairnessPolicyController` refresh path is registered and callable through `dfsrouteradmin`, controller swaps take effect for subsequent RPC fairness decisions, prior controllers are shut down cleanly, and fairness-handler accounting reflects the refreshed configuration rather than the stale one from process startup.

  '

===== rbf-fedbalance-link.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16255. RBF: Fix dead link to fedbalance document'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Router-based Federation documentation points readers to the FedBalance material when they need migration and balancing guidance. If that reference is broken, operators hit a dead end right in the middle of the documentation flow.


  ## Desired outcome

  The RBF documentation should link correctly to the FedBalance document so readers can navigate to the intended guidance without hunting for it manually. This is a documentation-only correction, so router behavior and admin commands stay unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The broken FedBalance link in the router federation documentation is corrected, readers can follow the documentation path successfully, and no product behavior changes beyond fixing the reference.

  '

===== rbf-trash-short-user.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16628 RBF: Correct target directory when move to trash for kerberos login user.'
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  In Router-based federation, a Kerberos-authenticated HDFS user deleting data through a mount point can be sent to the wrong trash location because the full principal is treated as the home-directory name.


  ## Desired outcome

  Router trash resolution should use the short username so a mounted delete lands under the same per-user trash hierarchy that other HDFS paths use.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A user authenticated as a principal such as `randomUser/dev@HADOOP.COM` finds deleted mounted files under the short-name trash location, for example `/user/randomUser/.Trash/Current/...`, instead of under a principal-form directory.

  '

===== redundant-semicolon-cleanup.yaml =====
title: 'HADOOP-18284. Remove Unnecessary semicolon '';'' '
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  A number of Hadoop sources still contain doubled semicolons that do not affect runtime behavior but make the codebase look noisier and less polished than it should.


  ## Desired outcome

  Remove those redundant semicolons across the affected modules while keeping all existing behavior unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The touched sources no longer contain the duplicated trailing semicolons, and there is no user-visible change beyond the style cleanup.

  '

===== removefromclusternodelabels-rename.yaml =====
title: 'YARN-11050. Typo in method name: RMWebServiceProtocol#removeFromCluserNodeLabels'
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Java callers of the RM and Router web-service layer have to live with a misspelled cluster-node-label removal method, even though the REST endpoint itself is already correct.

  ## Desired outcome

  The public Java API should use the corrected method name `removeFromClusterNodeLabels` while preserving the existing REST behavior and endpoint contract.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Code that interacts with the web-service interfaces sees the corrected method name, and the REST path remains exactly `/remove-node-labels`.

  '

===== remove-rs-api.yaml =====
title: 'HADOOP-18332: remove rs-api dependency as it conflicts with jsr311-api'
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Hadoop operators sometimes embed the web and REST components into environments that already carry their own JAX-RS libraries, and duplicate API jars can cause classpath conflicts before the service even starts.


  ## Desired outcome

  This dependency cleanup should remove the conflicting `rs-api` footprint so the build and packaged runtime align with the `jsr311-api` expectations already used elsewhere. It is internal compatibility work, so observable Hadoop behavior and public REST contracts should remain unchanged while startup becomes less fragile in mixed dependency environments.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected modules should no longer pull in the conflicting `rs-api` dependency, and packaging should continue to expose the same REST features without changing endpoints or response formats.

  '

===== revert-external-sps-jmx.yaml =====
title: 'Revert "HDFS-16488. [SPS]: Expose metrics to JMX for external SPS"'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators running the external Storage Policy Satisfier need the service itself to keep working, but they do not want a newly added JMX surface that is not ready to remain part of the supported management contract.

  ## Desired outcome

  External SPS should continue operating without exposing `ExternalSPSBeanMetrics` or the `ExternalSPSMXBean` management interface, and the attempted-item internals that were temporarily made public should go back to being internal implementation detail.

  ## Acceptance signals

  There is no JMX bean published for external SPS, while the command-line and runtime behavior of the service stay aligned with the pre-metrics implementation.

  '

===== revert-rbf-handler-allocation.yaml =====
title: 'Revert "HDFS-14750. RBF: Support dynamic handler allocation in routers"'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS federation operators need router fairness controls to stay on the stable, predictable model rather than exposing a newer dynamic handler-allocation surface that is not ready to keep.

  ## Desired outcome

  The router should fall back to the pre-existing fairness behavior, without dynamic allocation classes, adjustable semaphores, or the extra per-namespace capacity and accept/reject metrics introduced by that experiment.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Existing permit acquisition and available-handler reporting continue to work, but the dynamic handler-allocation feature surface is absent.

  '

===== rmadmincli-kerberos-retry.yaml =====
title: YARN-11210. Fix YARN RMAdminCLI retry logic for non-retryable kerbero…
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Administrators use `RMAdminCLI` against secured YARN clusters expecting retry logic to help with transient problems, but a bad Kerberos principal configuration is not recoverable and repeated retries only add delay and noise.


  ## Desired outcome

  The CLI should stop retrying when the failure is really a SASL/Kerberos setup error, and that condition should surface clearly as `Bad Kerberos server principal configuration` instead of being treated like a transient retryable transport problem. The retry policy distinction needs to be explicit enough that non-retryable SASL failures are excluded while ordinary remote failures keep their existing handling.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The retry helper should follow the `retryOtherThanRemoteAndSaslException` behavior, and a principal-parsing failure should surface as a `SaslException` with the message `Bad Kerberos server principal configuration`. RMAdminCLI should still retry the categories of failures that were intended to be retried before.

  '

===== router-app-attempt-rest.yaml =====
title: YARN-11228. [Federation] Add getAppAttempts, getAppAttempt REST APIs for Router.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Application-attempt diagnostics in federated YARN still have gaps: operators cannot ask the Router for the list of attempts or a single attempt record without contacting the owning ResourceManager directly.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Router should support both `getAppAttempts` and `getAppAttempt` as federated REST operations so attempt-level troubleshooting works the same way as other routed application APIs. Requests should still validate the application id up front and return the existing `Parameter error, the appId is empty or null.` message when that required identifier is missing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Given a valid application routed through the federation state store, the Router should return the application’s attempt list and individual attempt details through `getAppAttempts` and `getAppAttempt`. Missing or empty application ids should be rejected immediately with the established parameter-validation message.

  '

===== router-application-flow-refactor.yaml =====
title: YARN-11180. Refactor some code of getNewApplication, submitApplication etc.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  The YARN Router handles several application-submission flows with similar logic, and duplicated code makes retries, auditing, and failure paths harder to keep consistent.


  ## Desired outcome

  This is internal Router cleanup in a user-facing submission path: common logic around creating applications, submitting them, and related lookups should be consolidated so behavior stays consistent and easier to maintain. Existing client-visible semantics, audit events, and failure outcomes must remain the same while the shared flow becomes more uniform.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Application creation and submission should still route to active subclusters, preserve the same success and retry behavior, and continue producing the same externally visible results. The improvement should be reduced duplication and more consistent internal handling, not a new API surface.

  '

===== router-app-timeout-rest.yaml =====
title: YARN-11227. [Federation] Add getAppTimeout, getAppTimeouts, updateApplicationTimeout REST APIs for Router.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Federated YARN users can already inspect applications through the Router, but application-timeout management still requires talking directly to the owning ResourceManager.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Router should support `getAppTimeout`, `getAppTimeouts`, and `updateApplicationTimeout` so timeout inspection and updates work transparently in federation. These APIs should preserve the existing `AppTimeoutInfo` and `AppTimeoutsInfo` contracts, including fields such as timeout type, remaining seconds, and expiry time, and they should keep the current parameter-validation messages for missing `appId`, missing `type`, or null timeout payloads.


  ## Acceptance signals

  For a routed application with a lifetime timeout, `getAppTimeout` and `getAppTimeouts` should surface the timeout through `AppTimeoutInfo` values such as `ApplicationTimeoutType.LIFETIME`, remaining time, and an expiry string like `UNLIMITED` when that is the stored value. `updateApplicationTimeout` should return an `AppTimeoutInfo` echoing the updated expiry time, remaining seconds, and timeout type after the change is accepted.

  '

===== router-container-rest.yaml =====
title: YARN-11230. [Federation] Add getContainer, signalToContainer REST APIs for Router.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Federated YARN operators can inspect apps and attempts through the Router, but they still cannot fetch a single container record or send a signal to a container without going directly to the owning ResourceManager.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Router should implement `getContainer` and `signalToContainer` so those actions are routed to the application’s home subcluster automatically. Input validation needs to stay explicit: missing identifiers should be rejected with the existing `Parameter error, ... is empty or null.` style messages, and invalid signal names should come back as a BAD_REQUEST response that lists the valid `SignalContainerCommand` values.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After an application is submitted through the Router, a caller should be able to retrieve a non-null `ContainerInfo` for a specific attempt and container id via `getContainer`. `signalToContainer` should return OK for valid commands, return BAD_REQUEST for an invalid command string, and continue routing by deriving the home subcluster from the application id embedded in the container id.

  '

===== router-content-summary-snapshots.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-15225. RBF: Add snapshot counts to content summary in router.'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Users querying content summaries through the Router-based federation layer need snapshot counts to match what HDFS reports directly.

  ## Desired outcome

  Federated content summaries should include snapshot directory and snapshot file totals instead of dropping those counts during aggregation.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Router content-summary results carry the same snapshot counts that a direct namespace query would expose.

  '

===== router-fairness-timeout.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16671. RBF: RouterRpcFairnessPolicyController supports configurable permit acquire timeout'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  In Router-based federation, fairness throttling can protect overloaded nameservices, but a hardcoded permit wait time makes it difficult for operators to tune responsiveness for their own latency and throughput goals.


  ## Desired outcome

  Operators should be able to configure how long `RouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` waits to acquire a permit instead of being locked to a fixed one-second policy. The timeout must be controlled by `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`, measured in milliseconds, and invalid negative values should fall back to `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Permit acquisition should use the configured `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` value, including allowing an immediate timeout when the value is zero. Negative settings should not break the controller; they should log a warning and continue with `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`.

  '

===== router-getcontainers-federation.yaml =====
title: 'YARN-8900. [Router] Federation: routing getContainers REST invocations transparently to multiple RMs'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  In a federated YARN deployment, operators can already inspect application and attempt details through the Router, but container listings still stop at the individual ResourceManager boundary.


  ## Desired outcome

  When someone asks the Router for containers for an application attempt through `getContainers`, the Router should fan that request out to every active subcluster and return one merged `ContainersInfo` response instead of behaving as unimplemented. Invalid or unknown application or attempt identifiers should degrade cleanly to an empty container list rather than breaking the federated view.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A federated query for an application attempt spanning four active subclusters should come back with a single `ContainersInfo` whose `getContainers()` view contains all four containers. Requests for a nonexistent app, a malformed application id, or a malformed attempt id should return an empty `ContainersInfo`.

  '

===== router-node-label-rest.yaml =====
title: YARN-11220. [Federation] Add getLabelsToNodes, getClusterNodeLabels, getLabelsOnNode REST APIs for Router
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Federated YARN operators need cluster-wide visibility into label assignments, but the Router is missing several node-label REST views and cannot merge label data across subclusters.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Router should support `getLabelsToNodes`, `getClusterNodeLabels`, and `getLabelsOnNode` as federated REST APIs so administrators can inspect label state from one place. Merged responses should preserve the existing response objects such as `LabelsToNodesInfo`, `NodeIDsInfo`, `PartitionInfo`, and `NodeLabelsInfo`, including deduplicated node lists and aggregated partition resources when the same label appears in multiple subclusters.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A federated `getLabelsToNodes` response should merge repeated labels instead of overwriting them, and the merged `NodeIDsInfo` should carry the combined node list plus summed `PartitionInfo` resources. The Router should also return cluster labels containing `cpu` and `gpu`, and `getLabelsOnNode` should return labels `x` and `y` for `node1` while treating an unlabeled node like `node2` as an empty result rather than a failure.

  '

===== router-node-to-labels.yaml =====
title: YARN-11212. [Federation] Add getNodeToLabels REST APIs for Router.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  YARN federation administrators need to inspect node-to-label assignments across the whole deployment, but the Router still lacks a federated `getNodeToLabels` REST view.


  ## Desired outcome

  Calling `getNodeToLabels` on the Router should return a complete `NodeToLabelsInfo` map assembled from the active subclusters, rather than forcing operators to query each ResourceManager individually. The federated response should preserve the node-to-label structure clients already expect, including the `getNodeToLabels()` mapping keyed by node name.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A successful federated lookup should return a non-empty `NodeToLabelsInfo`, and callers should be able to read the merged labels through `getNodeToLabels()`. In the routed test scenario, the response should carry entries for `node1` and `node2`, with `CPU` attached to `node1` and `GPU` attached to `node2`.

  '

===== router-pipeline-utils.yaml =====
title: YARN-6572. Refactoring Router services to use common util classes for pipeline creations.
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  YARN Router request pipelines for the client, admin, and web layers all need the same interceptor-chain assembly rules, but duplicated setup logic makes failures inconsistent and harder to debug.


  ## Desired outcome

  This is internal consolidation work: interceptor chains should be created through one common utility so Router services keep identical behavior while configuration and instantiation errors are reported consistently. The shared helper needs to validate that each configured class is the right interceptor type and can be linked with `setNextInterceptor`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Pipeline creation should still honor the configured interceptor order and produce the same service behavior, but invalid classes or broken interceptor wiring should now fail through one common path with consistent `YarnRuntimeException` reporting. User-visible Router APIs and request routing outcomes should remain unchanged.

  '

===== router-rmwebprotocol-methods.yaml =====
title: YARN-8973. [Router] Add missing methods in RMWebProtocol.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  The Router’s RM web protocol surface is missing scheduler-configuration operations that operators already expect from a standalone ResourceManager.


  ## Desired outcome

  The RM web protocol should include the missing scheduler configuration endpoints so Router deployments can forward both reads and updates without forcing operators to bypass federation for those tasks. In particular, the protocol needs to support `updateSchedulerConfiguration` and `getSchedulerConfiguration` with the same request and response style users already expect.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A Router-backed RM web protocol implementation should expose `updateSchedulerConfiguration(...)` and `getSchedulerConfiguration(...)`, forwarding them through to the target web service. Existing Router endpoints should continue working unchanged.

  '

===== router-secure-login.yaml =====
title: YARN-6539. Create SecureLogin inside Router.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A secure YARN Router needs its own Kerberos login path rather than relying on borrowed assumptions from other daemons, otherwise federated services cannot be hardened cleanly.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Router should support an explicit secure-login configuration of its own, including dedicated keytab and principal settings, so operators can run the Router as a properly authenticated Kerberos service. The relevant configuration surface needs to include `ROUTER_KEYTAB` and `ROUTER_PRINCIPAL` and use them during Router startup.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A secured Router deployment should be able to authenticate using the Router-specific keytab and principal settings without depending on another daemon’s login path. Existing unsecured Router setups should continue to start without requiring Kerberos configuration.

title: HADOOP-18060.RPCMetrics increases the number of handlers in processing.

  ## Desired outcome

  RPC metrics should expose the current in-flight handler count through a dedicated metric instead of leaving this as an operational blind spot.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The metric name is `NumInProcessHandler`, it reports `0` when the server is idle, rises while handlers are actively processing calls, and falls back when those calls complete.

  '

title: HADOOP-18082.Add debug log when RPC#Reader gets a Call.
category: bugfix
requirement: 'HADOOP-18082.Add debug log when RPC#Reader gets a Call.


  ### Description of PR

  Log some information from the moment Call enters the RPC inside, which will help us understand more about Call.

  The records here should be in the form of logs. The priority of the logs should not be too high, and debugging is the best.

  Details: HADOOP-18082


  ### How was this patch tested?

  Corresponding to the test, the pressure is not large.

  '

===== rpc-request-rate-metrics.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18288. Total requests and total requests per sec served by RPC servers
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Hadoop operators need RPC server metrics that show both total request volume and current traffic rate, not just connection counts and timing summaries.


  ## Desired outcome

  The RPC metrics surface should expose cumulative and rate-based request views through `TotalRequests`, `TotalRequestsPerSecond`, `getTotalRequests()`, and `getTotalRequestsPerSecond()`, and the update cadence should remain configurable with `ipc.server.metrics.update.runner.interval`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After live RPC traffic, operators and dependent services can read a growing total request count together with a current per-second rate instead of finding those signals unavailable.

  '

===== s3a-bulk-delete-throttling-test.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18372. ILoadTestS3ABulkDeleteThrottling failing.
category: test
requirement: '## Context

  A scale test for S3A bulk delete throttling had become flaky because its setup and request configuration no longer matched the assumptions of the throttling path it was meant to exercise.


  ## Desired outcome

  This is test hardening work: the bulk-delete throttling load test should reliably configure throttling and page-size behavior before it runs so failures continue to indicate real regressions instead of test setup drift. Production bulk-delete behavior should not change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The updated test should consistently initialize the intended throttling configuration and bulk-delete page size before issuing requests, reducing false failures while still exercising the same deletion path.

  '

===== s3a-delete-on-exit.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18340. deleteOnExit does not work with S3AFileSystem
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Users expect `deleteOnExit` to work uniformly across Hadoop filesystems, but on S3A the registered paths were not actually being removed when the filesystem closed.


  ## Desired outcome

  S3A should honor `deleteOnExit` registrations the same way other Hadoop filesystems do, including for tracked paths that need to be deleted during shutdown. The filesystem should manage its own pending `deleteOnExit` set and use the same deletion semantics as normal deletes, without forcing callers to remember a separate cleanup path.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A path registered through `deleteOnExit` should be deleted when the S3A filesystem is closed, and the implementation should route that cleanup through the same deletion logic used for ordinary removals via `deleteWithoutCloseCheck`. If the path was never present, close should remain safe rather than turning the shutdown into a new failure.

  '

===== s3a-public-dataset-testutils.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18168. Fix S3A ITestMarkerTool dep. on purged public bucket, introduce PublicDatasetTestUtils
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The S3A public-dataset tests currently depend on a bucket layout that has been cleaned up, which makes previously stable requester-pays and marker-tool coverage unreliable. Test maintainers need those suites to point at a still-valid public dataset and to have one place that defines which public bucket and object should be used for each scenario.


  ## Desired outcome

  The S3A test utilities should provide a shared `PublicDatasetTestUtils` helper that supplies the configured public-dataset locations for cases such as requester-pays access and large public buckets with many objects. The default requester-pays path should move to a working public dataset, while still allowing environments to override those locations or skip the tests where requester-pays or AWS-specific assumptions do not apply.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The requester-pays coverage uses a valid public object again, marker-tool tests can obtain their public dataset locations through `PublicDatasetTestUtils`, configurable overrides remain available for different environments, and incompatible environments can skip these dataset-dependent tests instead of failing against a purged bucket.

  '

===== s3a-requester-pays-support.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-14661. Add S3 requester pays bucket support to S3A
category: feature
requirement: 'HADOOP-14661. Add S3 requester pays bucket support to S3A


  ### Description of PR


  This change introduces support for "requester pays" S3 buckets (HADOOP-14661).


  There was already some discussion and patches made available (e.g. #250), although the code base has changed a bit since then.


  In summary:


  - Add some information to the main S3A documentation

  - Add example of error and how to fix/configure to troubleshooting doc

  - Add options to configure requester pays in S3A (`fs.s3a.requester-pays.enabled`) when creating S3A filesystem, which uses S3ClientFactory to create a new S3Client also taking this option

  - Add the required header inside S3ClientFactory if option was configured

  - Remove unused configuration options for requester pays in RequestFactoryImpl

  - Add new integration test which talks to publicly available `usgs-landsat` bucket (new version, not old) which is configured to require requester pays ([''usgs-landsat'' on Registry of Open Data on AWS](https://registry.opendata.aws/usgs-landsat/index.html)).

  - Add information on how to configure the new tests in testing.md


  ### How was this patch tested?


  I created an EC2 instance and an S3 Bucket in eu-west-1 and ran the tests against the global S3 endpoint.


  ```

  mvn -Dparallel-tests -DtestsThreadCount=16 clean verify

  ```


  Note, the request pays specific tests introduced do not use the developer supplied bucket.


  ### For code changes:


  - [x] Does the title or this PR starts with the corresponding JIRA issue id (e.g. ''HADOOP-17799. Your PR title ...'')?

  - [x] Object storage: have the integration tests been executed and the endpoint declared according to the connector-specific documentation?

  - [x] If adding new dependencies to the code, are these dependencies licensed in a way that is compatible for inclusion under [ASF 2.0](http://www.apache.org/legal/resolved.html#category-a)?

  - [x] If applicable, have you updated the `LICENSE`, `LICENSE-binary`, `NOTICE-binary` files?

  '

===== s3a-vectored-iostats.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18227. Add input stream IOStats for vectored IO api in S3A.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using S3A vectored reads need the same visibility into performance and waste that they already have for ordinary stream reads, but vectored I/O currently leaves large observability gaps.


  ## Desired outcome

  S3A input streams should publish dedicated vectored-read IO statistics so operators can understand how often vectored reads happen, how many ranges are requested, and how many bytes are discarded as part of those reads. The counters must use the public statistic names `stream_read_vectored_operations`, `stream_read_vectored_read_bytes_discarded`, and `stream_read_vectored_incoming_ranges` so downstream tooling can consume them consistently.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Running vectored reads through S3A should update the new vectored IO counters alongside existing stream statistics. The statistics should be exposed through the standard IOStats surfaces with the exact metric names `stream_read_vectored_operations`, `stream_read_vectored_read_bytes_discarded`, and `stream_read_vectored_incoming_ranges`.

  '

===== setreplication-noop-editlog.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16531. Avoid setReplication writing an edit record if old replication equals the new value
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Some clients repeatedly call setReplication with the same replication value a file already has, which creates unnecessary NameNode work and extra edit-log traffic even though nothing is actually changing. At scale, these no-op requests add noise and overhead without improving file state.


  ## Desired outcome

  A set-replication request that does not change the current replication should still be treated as a successful operation from the caller''s perspective, but it should avoid writing an edit record or doing the heavier mutation path. Audit visibility should remain intact, and files should keep the same replication they already had.


  ## Acceptance signals

  No-op set-replication requests still succeed, the file''s replication remains unchanged, the NameNode avoids writing an unnecessary edit-log mutation for those no-op calls, and normal replication changes continue to follow the existing mutation path.

  '

===== shadedclient-test-jaxb.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18219. Fix shadedclient test failure
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Teams validating shaded Hadoop clients in integration environments need the shaded-client minicluster test setup to pull in the right JAXB dependency set.

  ## Desired outcome

  The test-classpath dependency selection should be corrected so shaded-client validation failures reflect real product issues instead of an invalid JAXB exclusion.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The shaded-client validation setup runs cleanly, with no user-visible change to shipped client APIs or runtime behavior.

  '

===== slow-node-latency-reporting.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16582. Expose aggregate latency of slow node as perceived by the reporting node
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators investigating slow peers need more than a list of suspicious DataNodes; they need to see which reporter observed the problem and how much latency was involved.

  ## Desired outcome

  The slow-peer report should carry the reporting node and observed latency for each slow node, and the tracker should return structured `SlowPeerLatencyWithReportingNode` entries instead of plain strings.

  ## Acceptance signals

  `getSlowPeersReport()` includes host identities together with latency values such as the reported 15.5, 14.5, or 18.7-style measurements, and tracker queries retain per-reporter latency data.

  '

===== slow-peer-jmx-reconfig.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16634. Dynamically adjust slow peer report size on JMX metrics
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  On busy HDFS clusters, administrators may need to increase or decrease the size of the slow peer report without restarting the NameNode, especially when cluster conditions change during an incident.


  ## Desired outcome

  `dfs.datanode.max.nodes.to.report` should be live reconfigurable so the updated limit immediately controls the slow peer report and also appears in the NameNode''s reconfigurable-properties listing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After live reconfiguration, the slow peer report expands or contracts without a restart, and administrative tooling shows `dfs.datanode.max.nodes.to.report` among the settings that can be reconfigured at runtime.

  '

===== slow-peer-outlier-metrics.yaml =====
title: HDFS-16595. Slow peer metrics - add median, median absolute deviation and upper latency limits
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators diagnosing slow peers need more than raw latency; they need the statistical context that made a peer an outlier.

  ## Desired outcome

  Slow-peer reporting should carry an `OutlierMetrics` record with `median`, `mad`, `upperLimitLatency`, and `actualLatency`, and those values should flow through reports, JSON output, and protobuf conversions.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Slow-peer reports and downstream consumers can see the exact metric values, not just the offending node names.

  '

===== sps-single-instance-start.yaml =====
title: 'HDFS-16499. [SPS]: Should not start indefinitely while another SPS process is running'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators can only run one Storage Policy Satisfier process at a time, but today a second start attempt can sit there retrying forever instead of telling the operator that SPS is already active. That makes automation and incident response confusing because a duplicate start looks hung rather than rejected.


  ## Desired outcome

  If SPS is started while another SPS instance is already running, the new attempt should fail immediately instead of retrying indefinitely. Operators should get a clear failure path they can act on, while normal SPS startup behavior remains unchanged when no competing process exists.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A duplicate SPS start exits promptly, a normal single SPS start still succeeds, and operators no longer see an endless retry loop when another SPS process already owns the work.

  '

===== vectored-stats-propagation.yaml =====
title: HADOOP-18392. Propagate vectored s3a input stream stats to file system stats.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  S3A vectored reads now collect stream-level counters, but filesystem-level statistics still do not reflect that activity, leaving operators with an incomplete top-level view.


  ## Desired outcome

  Vectored-read statistics gathered by S3A input streams should be propagated up into filesystem statistics so monitoring at the filesystem layer sees the same workload patterns as stream-level diagnostics. This should enrich observability only; vectored read behavior itself must not change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Running vectored reads through S3A should update both the input-stream counters and the aggregate filesystem statistics, including the vectored-read operation and range counters introduced for S3A. Existing vectored read success and error behavior should remain the same.

  '

category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Administrators use `RMAdminCLI` against secured YARN clusters expecting retry logic to help with transient problems, but a bad Kerberos principal configuration is not recoverable and repeated retries only add delay and noise.


  ## Desired outcome

  The CLI should stop retrying when the failure is really a SASL/Kerberos setup error, and that condition should surface clearly as `Bad Kerberos server principal configuration` instead of being treated like a transient retryable transport problem.   ## Acceptance signals

  The retry helper should follow the `retryOtherThanRemoteAndSaslException` behavior, and a principal-parsing failure should surface as a `SaslException` with the message `Bad Kerberos server principal configuration`.   '

title: 'HDFS-16671. RBF: RouterRpcFairnessPolicyController supports configurable permit acquire timeout'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  In Router-based federation, fairness throttling can protect overloaded nameservices, but a hardcoded permit wait time makes it difficult for operators to tune responsiveness for their own latency and throughput goals.


  ## Desired outcome

  Operators should be able to configure how long `RouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` waits to acquire a permit instead of being locked to a fixed one-second policy. The timeout must be controlled by `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`, measured in milliseconds, and invalid negative values should fall back to `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Permit acquisition should use the configured `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` value, including allowing an immediate timeout when the value is zero. Negative settings should not break the controller; they should log a warning and continue with `DFS_ROUTER_FAIRNESS_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`.

  '

title: HDFS-16470. Make HDFS find tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_find` command currently depends on Linux-only argument parsing, which makes the tool unavailable or unreliable on other platforms even though the underlying file search workflow is otherwise portable. Developers using the native client need the same basic find behavior regardless of operating system.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_find` should work cross-platform while preserving the existing command-line experience for searching from a start path, filtering by `-n`, and limiting traversal depth with `-m`. This is a portability fix, so the tool''s observable search behavior should stay the same while its option parsing becomes usable beyond Linux.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_find` runs on non-Linux platforms, still accepts the expected path and filtering options, and produces the same search results users would expect from the current Linux implementation.

  '

category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_ls` tool is tied to Linux-only option parsing today, which makes a basic file-listing command unnecessarily platform-specific for developers using the native client.   ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_ls` should become cross-platform without changing the user-visible command semantics, including normal listing and recursive traversal with `-R`. The portability work must preserve the current output behavior so users can keep the same scripts and expectations while gaining non-Linux support.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_ls` works on supported non-Linux platforms, still honors the existing path and `-R` behavior, and produces the same style of listing results users already rely on.

  '

title: HDFS-16472. Make HDFS setrep tool cross platform
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The native `hdfs_setrep` tool currently depends on Linux-only option parsing, which makes replication-management workflows unnecessarily platform-specific for teams using the native client on other operating systems. Operators and developers still need the same ability to change replication on files and recursively across directory trees regardless of platform.


  ## Desired outcome

  `hdfs_setrep` should work cross-platform while preserving its current command-line behavior for setting a target replication factor on a path and applying that change recursively when a directory is provided. This is a portability update, so the tool''s observable replication-changing behavior should remain the same while the argument parsing becomes usable beyond Linux.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `hdfs_setrep` runs on supported non-Linux platforms, still accepts the existing replication-factor and path arguments, continues to handle directory recursion as before, and changes replication in the same way users already expect from the Linux implementation.

  '

title: HADOOP-13144. Enhancing IPC client throughput via multiple connections per user
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Hadoop service running very high IPC call volumes to the same endpoint can bottleneck on a single client-side connection per user, even when the workload itself is highly parallel.


  ## Desired outcome

  Operators and framework code should be able to open more than one logical client connection for the same address, protocol, and user when they deliberately vary the connection identity, instead of being forced through one shared channel. The public RPC surface needs to make that possible by accepting a caller-supplied `Client.ConnectionId` in `RPC.getProtocolProxy(...)`, so advanced clients can spread traffic without forking the whole RPC stack.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Using `RPC.getProtocolProxy` with distinct `Client.ConnectionId` instances should yield independent client proxies and allow the same principal to drive parallel request streams to one server. Existing call semantics, security initialization, and retry behavior from the `ConnectionId` must remain intact.

  '

category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Native HDFS clients need the same richer open-file controls that are available on the Java side, including the ability to construct an open request, set required or optional parameters, and wait on the resulting asynchronous open. requirement: 'HDFS-16422. Fix thread safety of EC decoding during concurrent preads

title: 'HDFS-16479. EC: NameNode should not send a reconstruction work when the source datanodes are insufficient'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  In erasure-coded HDFS, the NameNode can currently schedule reconstruction work even when there are not enough usable source DataNodes to rebuild the missing data. That creates pointless work assignments which fail downstream and surface avoidable reconstruction errors on the DataNode side.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should skip issuing EC reconstruction work when the set of non-busy source DataNodes is insufficient to recover the missing stripes. Reconstruction should still be scheduled normally once enough valid sources are available, but impossible work should be filtered out before it is sent.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Reconstruction work is not dispatched when too few usable EC sources remain, no failing work item is generated for those impossible cases, eligible blocks are still scheduled once enough sources are available, and the affected under-reconstruction blocks remain tracked without triggering avoidable DataNode-side failures.

  '

title: HDFS-16528. Reconfigure slow peer enable for Namenode
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  NameNode operators may want to turn slow-peer tracking on or off while a cluster is running so they can manage diagnostic overhead without taking the NameNode down. Right now the `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` setting is not fully reconfigurable on the NameNode side, which makes that operational toggle less useful than related live-reconfig options.


  ## Desired outcome

  The NameNode should allow `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` to be reconfigured at runtime, with slow-peer tracking behavior updating immediately to match the new boolean value. When disabled, slow-peer reports and JSON output should stop surfacing collected data; when enabled again, the normal slow-peer tracker should resume without requiring a restart.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Administrators can reconfigure `dfs.datanode.peer.stats.enabled` on a live NameNode, the NameNode switches between enabled and disabled slow-peer tracking behavior immediately, disabled mode returns empty slow-peer results instead of stale data, and invalid non-boolean values are rejected as reconfiguration errors rather than being silently accepted.

  '
